title: Visual Checks of Electrical Items
blurb: A ten-second look at cables, plugs and sockets that spots most electrical faults before they cause a fire or shock.
siteNotes: Where "out of use" labels are kept
Who is the competent person to report faulty equipment to
How the venue records formal testing of portable appliances, if it does
legalNotes: Electrical equipment must be maintained so it does not give danger: Electricity at Work Regulations 1989, reg. 4. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/1989/635
Staff duty to take reasonable care: Health and Safety at Work etc. Act 1974, s.7.
CHECK: the trainer teaches user visual checks only. The session does not mention formal inspection or portable appliance testing, which is the venue's decision on risk; confirm the venue policy.
Visual checks of cable, plug, overheating signs, overloaded sockets and keeping water away follow HSE guidance on maintaining portable electrical equipment.

cards.title: Visual Checks of Electrical Items
cards.body:
By the end of this session you can:
- look over an item before you use it
- spot warning signs of a fault
- take a failed item out of use and report it

cards.title: A quick look prevents fires
cards.body: Faulty electrics cause fires and give people serious shocks, but a huge number of problems can be spotted with a simple look before you switch on. You do not need to be an electrician. You just need to know what a warning sign looks like and act on it.

cards.title: Look before you use
cards.body: Before you use equipment, take a couple of seconds to look it over. Smelling burning or hot plastic is an instant stop.

items.title: Overheating
items.text: Scorch marks or a brown plug.

cards.title: Sockets, leads and water
cards.body: Watch how things are set up as well as the item itself.

left.title: Do
items: Keep water and electrics well apart

right.title: Do not
items: Handle plugs or switches with wet hands

cards.title: Do not use it, do not fix it
cards.body: If an item fails your check, do not use it and do not try to fix it yourself. That is a job for a competent person.

cards.title: Trip hazard and easily damaged
cards.body: A cable trailing across a walkway is both a trip hazard and easily damaged. Keep cables out of walkways so people are safe and the cable is too.

cards.title: Remember
cards.body:
- Look before you use: cable, plug, overheating signs
- Burning or hot plastic smell: stop, unplug, report
- Failed? Do not use it or fix it. Label it out of use and report
- Never overload sockets or daisy-chain leads
- Keep water away from electrics

cards.q: A visual check should be done before you use an electrical item.
cards.why: A couple of seconds looking it over can spot a fault before it causes harm.

cards.q: A brown, discoloured plug is a sign of…
options: Normal wear that is fine to keep using
Overheating or a fault
Nothing to worry about
Just dirt from cleaning
cards.why: Scorch marks or a brown, discoloured plug are tell-tale signs of overheating.

cards.q: Name one thing you should look for on the CABLE of an item.
options: A neat, tidy coil of cable
A very long length of cable
Cuts, fraying or exposed wires
A bright, easy to see colour
cards.why: Check the cable for cuts, fraying or exposed wires.

cards.q: Overloaded sockets are a fire risk.
cards.why: Overloaded sockets and daisy-chained extension leads are a real fire risk.

cards.q: If an item fails the check, you should…
options: Repair it yourself with some tape
Keep using it, but carefully
Tell a guest to avoid using it
Unplug it, label it out of use and report it
cards.why: Do not fix it yourself. Switch off, unplug if safe, label it out of use and report it.

cards.q: You should never handle plugs or switches with wet hands.
cards.why: Keep water and electrics well apart.

cards.q: You smell burning or hot plastic from a device. What should you do?
options: Carry on until the job is done
Stop using it, unplug it and report it
Open a window and keep going
Wait to see if the smell goes
cards.why: Burning or hot plastic is an instant stop. Unplug it if safe and report it.

cards.q: Electrical repairs should be done by…
options: A competent person
Anyone with a screwdriver
Whoever is nearest
A guest who says they are an electrician
cards.why: Repairs are a job for a competent person, not for staff to try.

cards.q: A cable trailing across a walkway is both a trip hazard and easily damaged.
cards.why: Cables across walkways risk a fall and damage to the cable itself.

cards.q: Roughly how long does a basic visual check take?
options: About ten minutes
Around half an hour
A few seconds
A full morning
cards.why: A ten-second look could prevent a fire or save someone from a nasty shock.
